summary: Twin, Clallam County: a possible lookout known only from 1936 and 1942 maps. No structure or date found, and legal access needs a Rayonier permit.

access.note: Willhite's page says a Rayonier Timber Western Washington permit is required for legal access.

visit.trail_note: Willhite describes many overgrown roads around the summits and some off-trail walking near the high points.

evidence.supports: Twin is an old village below the mountain, on the Strait between the mouths of the Twin Rivers
evidence.quote: Twin is the name of an old village below the mountain, on the Strait located between the mouths of the Twin Rivers (East and West Twin Rivers).

evidence.supports: Only two hints of a possible lookout: 1936 Forest Service map and 1942 Metsker map
evidence.quote: Shown on the 1936 Forest Service recreation map and on the 1942 Clallam County Metsker map, these are the only two hints that a possible fire lookout existed at this point.

evidence.supports: Two 1942 USGS benchmarks make no mention of a lookout
evidence.quote: Two points have USGS benchmarks from 1942 but both made no mention of any lookout.

evidence.supports: Willhite searched seven locations and found little
evidence.quote: I searched 7 locations; none of them gave much evidence of anything ever being there.

evidence.supports: Exact spot of the possible lookout is unclear among several bumps on the mountain
evidence.quote: it is unclear just what spot it was at, since there are several bumps on the mountain

evidence.supports: Gentle topography at some spots means a tower need not be on the highest point
evidence.quote: But, given the gentle topography at some, a tower would not need to be at the highest point to have a good view.

evidence.supports: Trip report is by Eric Willhite
Forest Lookouts index lists the site under State, location 31N-10W-28
Forest Lookouts index lists the agency as State
Rayonier Timber permit is required for legal access
evidence.quote: A Rayonier Timber - Western Washington Permit is required to have legal access.

evidence.supports: Many overgrown roads thread around the summits
evidence.quote: There are many overgrown roads threading around the summits.

evidence.supports: Some off-trail walking to reach the high points
evidence.quote: There is a bit of off-trail to reach the highpoints

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The Forest Lookouts index lists the agency as State, but Willhite's page names a Rayonier Timber permit for legal access. The sources do not settle who manages the ground, so the story reports both and no agency is recorded in facts.

notes_for_editor: No source gives a build date, structure or removal date for a lookout at Twin. The only evidence is two map marks (1936 and 1942) and a null search, so the story is short and says so. The brief's agency 'State' is unsupported by Willhite and conflicts with his Rayonier permit note; left open. A Willhite Olympics list entry reads '<1936 Twin' with no explanation, which may be the same map evidence and was not used. The Rayonier permit is a legal-access condition, and the story does not give directions to the site.
